text: The most ridiculous carriage of a gentleman in his own house, is to see him bustling about the business of the place, whispering one servant, and looking an angry look at another: it ought insensibly to slide along, and to represent an ordinary current.
author: Michel de Montaigne
locator: Book III, Chapter IX, Of Vanity
translation: Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt, 1877
